title: Failed to Show Off
text: I used my Paralyze Lance to stun one of Itsuki’s companions who was about to swing a horizontal blow at me. Seeing this, Itsuki’s other companions began to protest.
“You damn Spear Hero! What are you doing?!”
“This is punishment for your disruptive behavior. From now on, anyone who disobeys my orders or acts arrogantly will be paralyzed without warning.”
“Don’t mess with us! We’re not putting up with this!”
“We’re not staying here! We’re not your slaves!”
“We’re going home!”
“Oink! Oink oink!”
“Then all of you will be paralyzed and reflect on your actions!”
“What are you doing!? S-stop it, aaaaaah!”

I paralyzed all of Itsuki’s companions—including the pig—just as they were trying to leave. I look down on Itsuki’s companions as they twitch and convulse on the ground. Sigh… Even though it’s Father’s order, this is a hassle. Or rather… I’m reminded of something Father said during the last loop.

“Motoyasu, you have a pretty radical streak, so be careful with your actions. Whatever you do, you should stop thinking that destroying a country or a religion will end conflict. It’ll fail, without a doubt. With any organization, if you just take out the leader, the remnants will just run amok, just like with Takt. In fact, it’ll just end with a new leader taking their place.”

I can really feel how true those words are. I thought that by eliminating the Smoked Meat, Itsuki’s group might become a little more reasonable, but the result hasn’t changed—it’s just that the leader has been replaced! The vacancies have been filled by some unknown guys, so their numbers haven’t actually decreased.

Is this what they call the “force of history”? Surely not… We’ve looped this many times before, but I never sensed anything like that. Well, I suppose the correct explanation is that, as a result of Itsuki’s subjective decision to fill the missing members, we’ve ended up with a similar outcome.
But… Father was right after all. Even if we eliminate Smoked Meat, it doesn’t seem like it’ll make much of a difference in the future.
I guess I’ll just tie them up and drag them along by force? So, I tied up the numb members of the Itsuki’s group and headed deep into the island.
“Agh…”
“Ugh…”

They’re groaning about something, but I don’t care. Actually, I’ve recruited these guys as allies, but will they even still be around in the future? Won’t they end up causing trouble and stop being allies anyway? Well, even if it’s just limited to this island, it’s a good way to show them how strong I am. It’s just the thing for regaining the levels I lost to the Three Heroes Church.
“Alright then! Let’s keep moving!”
I set off at a run, dragging Itsuki’s companions in a single file line deep into the island’s interior. Looking back, I could see a trail that looked like a worm’s path.
“Ugh—”
“Guh—”
“S-stop—I’m—I’m gonna die!”
It’s pretty chaotic, but there’s no way they’d die from something like this. If anyone gets seriously injured, I’ll at least cast a healing Magic spell on them.
“Ha ha ha ha! Aiming Lancer X!”

Deep in the island’s interior, just as the adventurers disappear from view, I start taking down the monsters that are closing in on us. Thanks to that, my level is rising rapidly. I’m sure Itsuki’s companions’ levels have gone up a bit too. Even the boss at the very back of the island is practically a pushover for me now—though it’s a bit of a hassle since it takes so long to respawn. In the meantime, I’ll keep wiping out the monsters that appear.
“Hahahahaha! Weak! Way too weak!”
“Ah… ah…”
For some reason, Itsuki’s companions have started looking at me with frightened eyes. What are they so scared of? It’s common knowledge that a Hero is far stronger than ordinary people.

With that, I wrapped up the day’s hunting in a flash. I could’ve even raised my party’s levels all the way to 80—the cap on Cal Mira Island—but the ones who’d recovered from paralysis tearfully begged me to head back because the sun was about to set, so we returned to the inn.
“If you run away, I won’t let you off easy.”
“Eek!?”

It seems Itsuki’s crew has finally grasped just how strong I am, and they’ve stopped acting all high and mighty. Do they need a little more training? Your so-called sense of justice is practically nonexistent—it might be good to thoroughly drill into them just how much Itsuki’s ridiculous sense of justice causes people trouble.

That’s what I thought, but since I don’t have any expectations for these guys, I decided against it. It’s pointless to say anything to a bunch of rotten-to-the-core scum. Well, anyway, the next day I dragged Itsuki’s crew around by force again and showed them just how strong I am. Thanks to that, I managed to level them all up to Lv. 80.
So, just as planned, I returned from the hunting grounds in the evening and headed back to the hotel on the main island…
“‘Hey, hey, hey!’”
It looks like Itsuki is surrounded by Filolial-sama and her friends, having a great time. I’d like to join in, too.
“Ah, it’s Lord Motoyasu!”
“That’s right! Kitamura!”
“Hey, hey, hey…”
Filolial-sama greeted me cheerfully when I arrived. Actually, so did Itsuki. He jumped right up and ran over to me.
“Motoyasu-san! Please take these kids away as soon as possible. I beg you!”

He looks like he’s about to cry. What’s going on? It’s kind of fun to see the usually arrogant and haughty Itsuki making such a childish face. Yuki-chan and the others also perked up and started circling around Itsuki again, asking him.
“‘Hey, hey, hey…’”
“Ugh…”
They look like they’re having a lot of fun. Maybe I’ll join in, too.
“Hey, hey, hey!”
“M-Motoyasu-san!?”
Itsuki looked at my face and slumped to his knees. What a pitiful sight.
“Why are you so terrified?”
“I-Itsuki-sama! You damned bird monsters!”
Just as one of Itsuki’s warrior companions, furious, took a step forward with a weapon in hand, I turned to face him.
“Ugh…”
At that moment, he seemed to freeze up. Where did all that bravado go? He couldn’t run away, yet there was no one to attack. That’s how it looked.
“S-someone, help me…”
Itsuki was whimpering.
“Yuki-chan, what happened? I never thought Itsuki would get this weak.”
“Well, you see—”
Yuki-chan began to tell us what had happened with Itsuki.
After my Father and I left, it seems his companions—including Keel—were told to wait in another room. Then, Itsuki came to the room where Yuki-chan and the others were waiting.
“Please go ahead and open the door.”
“Excuse me.”
Apparently, despite everything, Itsuki entered the room politely.
Well, after all, they’d crossed paths while they were both confined there. Even though they never actually fought, they’d exchanged a few words.
“Shall we introduce ourselves?”
When Yuki-chan broke the silence with that question, Itsuki snapped back to his senses.
“Then, let’s formally introduce ourselves. I’m Itsuki Kawasumi, the Bow Hero. I look forward to spending the next two days with you all.”
“I’m Yuki, in charge of Lord Motoyasu’s Filolial.”
“My name is Kou! Nice to meet you, Kawasumi.”
“…Luna.”
Kou and Luna introduced themselves to Yuki-chan.
“We’ve crossed paths a few times, but let’s fight together.”
“Understood. As Lord Motoyasu instructed, I’ll demonstrate our strength to Itsuki-sama.”
It seems Itsuki looked displeased at Yuki-chan’s words. He must be unhappy about having to ask someone else for guidance.
“Let’s get right to it and go level up. I’ll be adding you to my party, so please agree.”
“That’s right. It would be best if you properly understood just how strong we are.”
“Kou, this is boring—let’s go already!”
After forming their party, they reportedly left the room and walked straight toward the harbor.
On the way to the harbor, Luna-chan apparently transformed into her Filolial Queen form and stared intently at Itsuki from behind several times.
“W-what is it?”
Luna-chan slowly reached out to stroke Itsuki’s head, but perhaps because he didn’t like her attitude, Itsuki brushed her hand away.
“What’s with that all of a sudden!”
“Sigh… You really aren’t as cute as I thought.”
“So what’s your point!”
Itsuki said this with a look of annoyance, but this is Luna-chan, after all. She was probably trying to figure out if Itsuki was petite and cute.
“Well then, let’s go. Itsuki-sama, please ride on our backs.”
“Huh? Ride…?”
Itsuki pointed at the small boat, but Yuki-chan and the others transformed into their Filolial forms and slowly dove into the sea.
“What’s the matter? Come on, let’s get moving.”
“Ah… Sigh.”

Itsuki scratched his head nervously, then climbed onto Yuki-chan’s back, and they began their journey to the hunting grounds. Man, I’m so jealous. I’ll make sure to get a ride myself once I’m free to move around.
“Well then, let’s check while we’re on the move. My level is 70. What about you two?”
“Eh…”
It seems Itsuki was left speechless as he rode on Yuki-chan’s back, gliding gracefully toward the island like a waterfowl.
“I-I see…”
It’s a shame he hadn’t broken through his level cap yet. If they don’t take down Takt quickly, things are going to get tough from here on out.
